# Rules, checks and gates

## Maturity

An element's supported rung is the highest one for which every `error` rule from that rung down holds, capped by the gates. A claim above that is an error.

## Coverage rules written by hand

### `ACT`

| Rule | From | Severity | Requires | When it fails | Conditions |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `COV-ACT-role` | `specified` | error | at least 1 outgoing `holds` to `ROLE` | holds no role | where {"kind":"human"}; module identity |
| `COV-ACT-uses` | `specified` | warn | at least 1 incoming `audience` | does nothing in the product: no feature, flow or message is for it |  |

## Checks

Coded checks for what a declarative rule cannot say. `from` is the rung an element must claim before the check applies to it.

### SCH

| Check | Severity | From | Reads | What it checks |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `SCH-project` | error | any |  | pds.yaml has only known keys, a known profile, adoption and modules, and every rule, advisory check or probe it switches off exists, may be switched off (an error-level check may not) and has a stated reason. |
| `SCH-frontmatter` | error | any |  | A record opens with a frontmatter block that parses as PDS-YAML. |
| `SCH-id-form` | error | any |  | An id is a known type prefix, a hyphen and a lowercase kebab slug (FEAT-send-invoice). |
| `SCH-id-file` | error | any |  | The file is named after the id and sits in the folder of its family. |
| `SCH-id-unique` | error | any |  | No two records share an id. |
| `SCH-envelope` | error | any |  | A record has an id and a title, and only keys defined for its type. |
| `SCH-field-type` | error | any |  | Every field value matches its declared type, including enum values. |
| `SCH-anchor` | error | any |  | The anchor exists and is of a type this element may live under. |
| `SCH-singleton` | error | any |  | There is exactly one product, and at most one tenancy model. |
| `SCH-rel-key` | error | any |  | A key under rel is a known relation. A derived inverse name is refused with a pointer to the other side. |
| `SCH-rel-pair` | error | any |  | A relation connects types its definition allows, and its attributes are valid. |
| `SCH-block` | error | any |  | A structured block parses and carries the keys its type requires. |
| `SCH-section` | error | any |  | A heading appears once in a record. |
| `SCH-summary` | error | any |  | A summary is one line of at most 200 characters. |

### REF

| Check | Severity | From | Reads | What it checks |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `REF-target` | error | any |  | Every relation target, field reference and block reference names an existing element of an allowed type. |
| `REF-mention` | error | any | `mentions` | Every [[ID]] in prose names an existing element. |
| `REF-anchor-cycle` | error | any |  | Following anchors upward always ends at the product. |
| `REF-retired` | warn | any |  | An active element does not depend on a retired one, except to record history (supersedes, concerns, evidenced_by). |
| `REF-depth` | warn | any |  | Domains and capabilities nest at most three levels deep. |

### COH

| Check | Severity | From | Reads | What it checks |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `COH-flow-shape` | error | `outlined` |  | In a flow, step ids are unique; entry and every next or branch target exist; each step has exactly one of next, decide, end or call. |
| `COH-flow-reach` | error | `specified` |  | Every step of a flow is reachable from its entry and every path reaches an end. A loop with no way out is a warning. |
| `COH-flow-ends` | warn | `specified` |  | A flow of an important or critical feature has at least one success end and one failure or abort end. |
| `COH-flow-refs` | error | `specified` | `touches`, `governed_by`, `accesses`, `emits`, `drives`, `depends_on`, `audience` | A step's actor, screen, rule, entity, event, state-machine transition and called flow exist and are of the right type; moves names a real transition. |
| `COH-flow-size` | warn | any |  | A flow has at most 25 steps. Longer ones are split into called flows. |
| `COH-stm-shape` | error | `specified` |  | A state machine has exactly one initial state; every transition names defined states; terminal states have no way out; every state is reachable. |
| `COH-stm-driven` | warn | `verifiable` | `drives` | Every transition either names a system trigger or is moved by at least one flow. |
| `COH-ent-attributes` | error | `specified` | `associates` | Attribute names are unique; associations point at entities; an entity that says it holds no personal data has no personal attribute; one holding personal data is classified confidential or higher. |
| `COH-payload` | error | `specified` |  | Payload field names are unique and an event that says it carries no personal data has no personal field. |
| `COH-journey` | error | `specified` | `spans`, `touches` | Journey stage ids are unique; stage flows and touchpoints exist; feeling is a number from 1 to 5. |
| `COH-plan-entitlements` | error | `specified` | `grants` | A plan lists only entitlements that exist, with values that fit each one's kind, and a price whose model, amount and interval agree. |
| `COH-rule-examples` | error | `specified` |  | A rule has worked examples, at least one positive and at least one negative or edge case, each with a given and a then. |
| `COH-screen-states` | error | `specified` |  | A screen that shows data defines at least its loading, empty and error states. |
| `COH-facets` | error | any |  | A feature does not declare false a facet the graph shows to be true. |
| `COH-role-limits` | error | `specified` |  | A role's minimum holders do not exceed its maximum, and assignable_by never forms a loop. |
| `COH-dependency-cycle` | warn | any | `depends_on` | Hard dependencies between capabilities or features do not form a cycle. |
| `COH-supersedes` | error | any | `supersedes` | Supersession never loops; the element replaced is deprecated or retired. |
| `COH-release-scope` | warn | any | `includes` | A release that is planned or in progress does not include a retired element. |
| `COH-tier-order` | warn | any |  | A child is not more critical than the element it sits under. |
| `COH-qst-answer` | error | any |  | A question that is no longer open is not still marked blocking, and an open question carries no answer. |

### QLT

| Check | Severity | From | Reads | What it checks |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `QLT-req-form` | warn | `outlined` |  | A requirement is one sentence with 'shall' and begins with The, When, While, If or Where. |
| `QLT-req-measurable` | error | `specified` |  | A quality requirement contains a number, a unit or a threshold that can be tested. |
| `QLT-req-single` | warn | `outlined` |  | A requirement states one thing: it does not join several obligations with 'and' after 'shall'. |
| `QLT-vague` | warn | `outlined` |  | Requirements, rules and definitions avoid unmeasurable words such as fast, easy, intuitive, robust, seamless, user-friendly, flexible, scalable, appropriate, and so on. |
| `QLT-placeholder` | error | `specified` |  | No TBD, TODO, XXX, lorem ipsum or unfilled <angle-bracket> placeholder remains in an element that claims to be specified. |
| `QLT-gherkin` | error | `specified` |  | A test's gherkin block has a Scenario with Given, When and Then in order, and no scenario is empty. |
| `QLT-summary` | warn | `outlined` |  | A summary says more than the title does. |
| `QLT-term-avoid` | warn | any |  | Prose does not use a word a glossary term lists as one to avoid. |
| `QLT-term-duplicate` | error | any |  | Two glossary terms in the same scope do not share a name or an alias. |
| `QLT-duplicate` | warn | any |  | Two elements of one type under the same anchor do not have near-identical titles. |
| `QLT-sys-reference` | warn | any |  | A system component stays a reference: its body is short and points to the design documents in links. |
| `QLT-title` | warn | any |  | A title is at most 80 characters and does not end in a full stop. |

### GOV

| Check | Severity | From | Reads | What it checks |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `GOV-claim` | error | any |  | An element does not declare a maturity above the one its definition supports. The finding names every failing rule. |
| `GOV-approval-hash` | error | any |  | An approved element's content still matches the hash that was approved. The approval of a feature or capability is bound to everything it covers (itself and what is anchored beneath it that no nested unit covers), so an edit to any of it shows here. After an edit it must be approved again. |
| `GOV-approval-authority` | error | any |  | Approval names a human approver listed in pds.yaml, and a date. An agent never approves. |
| `GOV-tier1-approval` | warn | any |  | Every approval that policy asks for exists. Policy asks for one when a critical (tier 1) element claims specified or better. The unit of approval is the unit of build: one approval of a feature covers everything anchored beneath it, and one of a capability covers what is shared at its level, so the elements inside a unit are not asked separately. |
| `GOV-skeleton` | error | any |  | An element whose origin is skeleton claims no more than outlined and is not approved until a person has confirmed it. |
| `GOV-lifecycle-note` | error | any |  | A deprecated or retired element says why and what replaces it. |
| `GOV-freshness` | warn | any |  | An approved element has been reviewed within its tier's review period. |
| `GOV-overdue` | warn | any |  | An assumption past its validate_before date, or a question past its due date, is still open. |
| `GOV-blocking-question` | error | any |  | An element does not claim specified while an open blocking question concerns it. |

### PRB

| Check | Severity | From | Reads | What it checks |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `PRB-disposition` | error | any |  | A probe disposition is addressed, na or deferred; na and deferred give a reason, and deferred names a question or a date. |
| `PRB-addressed` | error | any |  | An addressed probe names the elements that address it, and they exist. |
| `PRB-unknown` | warn | any |  | Every probe named on a feature exists. |

## Gates

| Gate | Caps at | Meaning |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `GATE-blocking-question` | `outlined` | While an open blocking question concerns an element, or any element that anchors under it, the element cannot be computed above outlined. |
| `GATE-skeleton` | `outlined` | An element whose origin is skeleton cannot be computed above outlined, however complete it looks, until a person confirms it and the origin changes. |
| `GATE-retired` | `none` | A retired element is excluded from coverage and from the gap queue. |
